frames.narration: A customer pays. The provider sends an event to the shop's registered URL, with a signature header made from a shared secret.
The endpoint recomputes the signature and checks the timestamp is recent. A forged or replayed request would be rejected here.
It checks the event id. evt_9 has not been handled before, so it records it and hands the work to a queue.
The endpoint replies 200 immediately. The real work (marking the order paid, shipping) happens afterwards.
Another event arrives while the shop's server is down. The provider gets no answer and treats it as failed.
The provider retries later on a growing schedule: 1 minute, 5 minutes, 30 minutes. When the shop is back, a retry succeeds.
Suppose the shop's 200 for evt_9 was lost. The provider sends evt_9 again. The endpoint sees the id was already handled, replies 200 and does nothing, so the order ships once.
